Cats meowed more when a person was present, suggesting they direct the sound at humans who can help. In a Brazilian study led by Naila Fukimoto of the University of São Paulo, 38 cats faced an unreachable treat. They meowed 86 times with a person in the room, versus 20 times alone, and often looked between the person and the container.

Published in Animal Behaviour, the findings support the idea that meows are aimed at people. The authors caution that the study involved a small group of food-focused, vocal cats and just one scenario, so not every meow is a demand.

Fukimoto, N., Albuquerque, N., & Savalli, C. (2026). Domestic cats (Felis catus) direct meows at humans during an unsolvable task. Animal Behaviour. DOI: 10.1016/j.anbehav.2026.123756

🌍 Iranian Mission in Vienna: Aggression cannot be erased by resolutions

📌 London, IRNA – Iranian Permanent Mission to International Organizations in Vienna criticized the legal and technical foundations of the International Atomic Energy Agency's reports on Iran, calling on the IAEA Board of Governors to address the consequences of military attacks against the country's nuclear facilities.

The Iranian mission stated that the IAEA has based its reports on Iran on resolutions adopted by the Board of Governors that are technically and legally flawed, were adopted through the abuse of decision-making procedures, and contain findings that exceed the Agency's statutory mandate.
​
Referring to remarks by IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, the mission emphasized that, as Grossi himself acknowledged, attacks on Iran's safeguarded nuclear facilities have created unprecedented circumstances, disrupted inspection activities, and forced the Agency to withdraw its inspectors.
​
The mission stressed that these circumstances also require Iran's security concerns to be taken into account.
​
"The United States removed the aggression from biased resolutions, but its consequences cannot be erased from reality. Facts do not disappear simply because politics demands it," the mission stated.
​
In another part of its message, the Iranian mission emphasized that returning to normal conditions requires addressing the factors responsible for creating the current situation.
​
"Normal safeguards implementation cannot and will not resume under abnormal circumstances," it stressed.
​
The mission concluded by emphasizing that the IAEA Board of Governors must address the root causes of the current situation.
​
However, it added that this is an impossible task because the Board includes the aggressor among its members.

Crypto Idea

SoftBank is probably best known for its stories involving WeWork and some of the world's biggest companies. And it looks like the holding company has now reached a point where AI is no longer just a story about rising asset valuations, but a story about real debt.

The company has made a massive bet on AI. It has invested or committed to invest around $65 billion in OpenAI alone, while OpenAI and Arm now account for roughly three-quarters of the value of its key assets.

The problem is that a significant portion of this bet is being financed with debt. In September, SoftBank issued $11.1 billion in bonds, the largest high-yield corporate bond offering in history. Some of those bonds carried yields of nearly 10% annually.

And the market is already getting nervous. SoftBank shares have lost nearly half their value since the beginning of September, while the cost of insuring against a potential debt default has reached its highest level in four years.

The really uncomfortable part begins if AI asset valuations continue to fall. That would mean collateral loses value, borrowing becomes more expensive, and the company may have to sell assets to reduce its debt. And SoftBank owns a significant stake in Arm, is one of OpenAI's largest investors, and is financing massive AI infrastructure projects.

That's why SoftBank's problems could quickly stop being the problems of just one company. 
The pressure could spread to Arm, private AI company valuations, data centers, and eventually the entire tech market.

On Tuesday, November 10, SoftBank will release its latest quarterly earnings report. The main things to watch are its debt, cash position, and how the company plans to keep financing its AI bet.

Because if the next major AI crisis starts not with a stock market sell-off, but with debt problems at the biggest borrowers, SoftBank is one of the first places to look for signs of trouble.
